lesson.title: Now the Line Is Open
lesson.hook: The net player moves early toward the middle. This serve gives you enough time to see the lane they have left.

lines.A: You give the ball room and prepare together for another reply.

drlA.take: When they leave the line, read the opening.

drlA.why: The same return target is not right for every net position. The line is available here because the net player moves early and your contact is manageable. It is not a command to hit a low-percentage winner.

lesson.pairPlan: If their net player crosses early and the serve gives us time, use the vacated line with margin. Keep covering the next ball.

comparison.summary: All four players stay involved. This is one illustrated continuation, not a predicted result.
comparison.intro: Same incoming ball. Compare how the first call changes the pair’s next job.

summaries.10: The pair’s first move fitted. The next contact still needed margin.
summaries.11: You read the pair’s coverage and gave the next ball room.
summaries.01: Your next shot had margin. Review the first coverage call together.
summaries.00: Review the first call, then choose a target that fits the next contact.

lesson.completionIntro: One call. Two responsibilities. Take the plan to your next match.

pro.label: From the coaching court
pro.moment: The LTA links forward and sideways movement to pressure and coverage. A net player can close one lane while opening another; the returner has to see the trade-off.
pro.read: The same return target is not right for every net position. The line is available here because the net player moves early and your contact is manageable. It is not a command to hit a low-percentage winner.

drill.name: Rehearse as a pair
drill.how: Repeat the return drill with an occasional early crossing move. Reward recognising the changed lane and recovering; do not award extra points for outright winners.
